claims.text: Integrating active learning with high-throughput experimental feedback can rapidly identify refractory high-entropy alloy compositions.
The identified RHEA compositions can combine intrinsic strength, ductility, and low weight.
Active-learning-designed compositions will outperform compositions designed through traditional thermo-kinetic or simulation-based methods.
Conventional thermo-kinetic analysis and simulation are used to design baseline RHEAs over a broad range of multi-principal refractory-element compositions.
A closed-loop active learning algorithm can iteratively suggest new compositions using results from high-throughput synthesis and rapid property characterization.
The proposed experiments use rapid thermal processing at approximately 1200 °C for durations ranging from minutes to hours.
The proposed compositional search varies constituent concentrations within example ranges of 5–40 atomic percent.
RHEA phase distribution and grain size evolve with alloy composition and processing conditions.
Phase distribution and grain size mediate the mechanical properties of the alloys.
Real-time experimental feedback progressively refines the machine-learning algorithm's training data.
Iterative feedback narrows the search space toward compositions that optimize strength, ductility, and low weight.
The iterative active learning process minimizes computational load.
The iterative process develops predictive composition–property relationships.
Active-learning-driven design will yield RHEAs with significantly improved mechanical performance relative to conventionally designed baseline alloys.
Any anticipated improvements are limited to the specified rapid processing and testing conditions.
Results obtained in the proposed framework may not generalize to other processing regimes or non-refractory alloy systems.
